title: Why does 99 divide a three digit number minus its reverse?
description: The trick is tried on a three digit number, three hundred fifty two, and its reverse. Letters for the three digits show the middle digit cancels and the result is ninety nine times the gap between the first and last digits. Keeko doubts this and thinks the result is always ninety nine.
teaching_notes: One idea: write the three digit number by place value, subtract the reverse, the tens cancel and the ninety nines group together. Watch for students who think one example fixes the result for every number.

source: Take 352, reverse it to 253 and subtract. Show with letters
video_script.why: The child sees that the same letter method works for three digit numbers, the middle digit cancels, and the result is ninety nine times the gap between the first and last digits.
video_script.substitution: Write the number as 100a + 10b + c and its reverse as 100c + 10b + a with a larger than c, subtract, cancel the tens, group the ninety nines, and check with 352.
video_script.anchor: the number 352 and its reverse 253 on the board, then the same two numbers written with letters
video_script.wrong_answer: the result is always ninety nine
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko sees that three hundred fifty two gives ninety nine and says the result is always ninety nine, so one example is taken for every number.
video_script.payoff_line: The result is ninety nine times the first digit take away the last digit

final_answer.spoken: ninety nine times eigh take away see

maths_rules: a three digit number with digits a, b, c is 100a + 10b + c; the reverse is 100c + 10b + a; a > c
(100a + 10b + c) − (100c + 10b + a) = 100a − a + c − 100c = 99a − 99c, the tens cancel
99a − 99c = 99 × (a − c), so the result is divisible by 99
slip: 631 − 136 = 495 = 99 × 5, so the result is not always 99
video_script.design: One idea: letters for the three digits make the middle digit cancel and the ninety nines group together. The number and its reverse stay on the board. Keeko's doubt is that the result is always ninety nine.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; the number 352 written, its reverse 253, and 352 − 253 = 99, 99 ÷ 99 = 1

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.ask: the words every three digit number? appear

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>Your book uses letter numbers to explain tricks and puzzles. Here is one with three digits.
<bookmark mark='pick'/>Take three hundred fifty two and reverse the digits to get two hundred fifty three.
<bookmark mark='take'/>Three hundred fifty two take away two hundred fifty three is ninety nine. Ninety nine divides ninety nine one time, with nothing left over.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Will ninety nine divide the result for every three digit number like this?

beats.on_screen: the numbers stay on the board while the child thinks

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: 352 = 100 × 3 + 10 × 5 + 2; letters: hundreds digit a, tens digit b, ones digit c, number = 100a + 10b + c, with a larger than c

marks.letters: the digits become the letters a, b and c, and the number becomes 100a + 10b + c
marks.order: the number is marked as the larger one and the reverse as the smaller one

beats.colours: hundreds, tens and ones parts in three colours
narration: <bookmark mark='place'/>Three hundred fifty two is three hundreds, five tens and two ones.
<bookmark mark='letters'/>Use letters for the digits. Eigh is the hundreds digit, bee is the tens digit and see is the ones digit.
<bookmark mark='order'/>The first digit is larger than the last, so the number is the larger one. We take the reverse away from it.

beats.on_screen: Given: a three digit number with digits a, b, c; a larger than c

marks.given: the number and its digits are written with letters

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a three digit number with digits eigh, bee and see. The first digit, eigh, is larger than the last digit, see.

beats.on_screen: To show: the number take away its reverse is divisible by 99

marks.find: the aim is written on the board

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to show that ninety nine divides the number take away its reverse.

marks.num: 100a + 10b + c is written for the number
marks.rev: 100c + 10b + a is written for the reverse

narration: <bookmark mark='num'/>Step one, write both numbers by place value. The number is one hundred times eigh, plus ten times bee, plus see.
<bookmark mark='rev'/>The reverse is one hundred times see, plus ten times bee, plus eigh.

marks.cancel: the two 10b terms are crossed out

beats.colours: the a terms and the c terms in two colours, the 10b terms greyed
narration: <bookmark mark='take'/>Step two, take the reverse away from the number.
<bookmark mark='cancel'/>The tens parts are the same, so they cancel.
<bookmark mark='nines'/>One hundred eigh take away eigh is ninety nine eigh. See take away one hundred see is minus ninety nine see.

marks.common: the common 99 is pulled out in front
marks.div: the words 99 divides it are written

beats.colours: the common 99 in the accent colour
narration: <bookmark mark='common'/>Step three, take out ninety nine, because both parts have it. That leaves ninety nine times eigh take away see.
<bookmark mark='div'/>Ninety nine is a factor of the result, so it divides the result.

beats.on_screen: Step 4, check with 352: a − c = 3 − 2 = 1 and 99 × 1 = 99
narration: <bookmark mark='gap'/>Step four, check with three hundred fifty two. Eigh take away see is three take away two, which is one.
<bookmark mark='nine'/>Ninety nine times one is ninety nine, the same as before.

beats.on_screen: Answer: result = 99 × (a − c), always divisible by 99

marks.ans: the answer result = 99 × (a − c) is boxed
marks.gap: a − c glows as the gap between the outer digits

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The result is ninety nine times the first digit take away the last digit.
<bookmark mark='gap'/>Ninety nine always divides it, and the middle digit plays no part.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the numbers
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows 99; 631 − 136 = 495 appears beside it and 99 is struck out; 495 = 99 × 5

marks.fix: 495 = 99 × 5 is written, with the gap 6 − 1 = 5 glowing

beats.colours: the wrong idea in the warning colour
narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the result is always ninety nine, because three hundred fifty two gave ninety nine.
<bookmark mark='test'/>Try six hundred thirty one. Take away one hundred thirty six and we get four hundred ninety five.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>That is ninety nine times five, and five is six take away one. Ninety nine divides it, but the result changes.
